title: A covenant on every run of years

blocks.text: A port authority finances its capital plan through a bond program, and the bond covenant now limits how fast it may spend: any `k` consecutive years of the plan together may spend at most `cap`. The model in `rolling.py` holds only the whole plan to one cap, so a plan can still crowd its spending into a few years.
The model so far, with $`Y = (y_1, \dots, y_n)`$ the plan's years in order and $`\text{spend}_y`$ the given linear expressions in the plan's 0/1 variables:

Write the covenant first in this notation: which sets of years it caps (say exactly which first years a window may have), and one row per such set, with its quantifier and a label. Then write `add_rolling_caps(model, spend, years, k, cap)` to add those rows and return them in a dict keyed by each window's first year. If the plan has fewer than `k` years, no window fits and there is no row. `add_plan_cap` shows the old row; the tests call your function alone.
The tests fix a plan and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct formulation passes. About five lines.

cases.says: a plan whose every run of k years fits the cap is allowed, and one that breaks the first run is refused
the runs overlap: each year starts one, not every k-th year
the last run of k years ends in the plan's last year
each run holds k years, so a plan can fit every shorter run and still break one
